_comment: DimensionCanon — real-world canonical dimensions for generated objects, in CUBES (1 cube = 1 m). Sibling of character_design_constraints.json. Furniture HEIGHTS are anthropometric (body-derived, period-stable, character-bounded); TYPES/footprints are medieval. Every archetype carries a primary `source` + a per-value `sources` map (the grounding rule). 'INFERRED' = reasonable estimate, low confidence; 'POST-MEDIEVAL' = anachronistic for the medieval frame, flagged. See docs/structure-generation/StructureGenerationV2.md + docs/structure-generation/StructureBrief.md.
_units: cubes (metres). 'tol' = tolerance in cubes. 'anchors' = required interaction-point ids.

sources.post_spacing: wood-fence posts 6-8 ft = 1.8-2.4 m (American Fence Assoc.)
sources._note: MEDIEVAL equivalent = paling fence; picket is the same form

sources.height: privacy fence 6 ft (6-8 ft range) = 1.8-2.4 m (freedomfenceandrailing.com)
sources._note: MEDIEVAL equivalent = wattle hurdle / close paling

sources.height: INFERRED ~4 ft post-and-rail (no clean height source)
sources.post_spacing: post spacing from AFA fencing guidance

gate_garden.description: Garden gate in a fence line
gate_garden.source: garden gate sized to the fence + character clearance

sources.clear_w: matches a 36 in exterior door clear width 0.9 m (doors.com)

chair_dining.description: Dining/side chair (medieval: rare, a lord's seat)

sources.seat_top: dining chair seat 17-20 in = 0.43-0.51 m, body-derived/period-stable (hernest.com; lagoonfurnitures.com)

tavern_bar.source: bar counter 42 in; bar top 20-30 in deep (barstoolcomforts.com; morfurniture.com)

sources.height: dedicated bar counter 42 in = 1.07 m, body-derived/ergonomic (barstoolcomforts.com; morfurniture.com). The 1/9 m micro grid lands at 1.111 m (nearest layer, +0.04).
sources.depth: bar top depth 18-30 in = 0.46-0.76 m; ~24 in = 0.6 m (dimensions.com/element/bar-details)
sources._note: POST-MEDIEVAL / fantasy-tavern: a fixed bar counter is later than the medieval frame (period taverns served from barrels). Ergonomic heights are grounded; the bar FORM is a deliberate fantasy-tavern choice (user-requested).

back_bar.source: INFERRED wall shelving ~1.8-1.9 m (cf. bookshelf 1.8 m)

sources.height: INFERRED back-bar ~1.8-1.9 m wall shelving (cf. bookshelf archetype 1.8 m)
sources._note: POST-MEDIEVAL / fantasy-tavern back bar — no period source; dims INFERRED from shelving.

bar_stool.source: bar stool seat 30 in for a 40-42 in counter (barstoolcomforts.com; dimensions.com)

sources.height: bar-stool seat 30 in = 0.76 m for a 42 in bar (10-12 in seat-to-counter gap), body-derived (barstoolcomforts.com; dimensions.com). Built 0.778 m (nearest 1/9 m).
sources.width: bar-stool seat width 16-22 in; this is a COMPACT stool at ~17 in = 0.44 m, slim end of the range (webstaurantstore.com/article/1045/bar-stool-dimensions.html; dimensions.com/element/stool-heights)
sources.depth: SQUARE seat: depth = width 0.44 m by construction; bar-stool seat depth runs ~13-18 in (webstaurantstore.com)
sources._note: POST-MEDIEVAL: a tall bar stool pairs with the fantasy-tavern bar; ergonomic dims grounded.

candle_stand.source: medieval standing pricket candlesticks / floor candelabra (period-appropriate); height INFERRED

sources.height: INFERRED floor candelabra ~1.0-1.5 m (no precise source); medieval standing pricket candlesticks existed (period-appropriate, not anachronistic)

wall_lantern.source: wall sconce mount 60-72 in (1800lighting.com); taper sconce ~12.5 in tall (amazon)

sources.height: INFERRED ~0.4 m (UNVERIFIED) — an enclosed lantern body is bulkier than a bare sconce arm; cf. (not equal to) a taper WALL SCONCE 12.5 in = 0.32 m (WHW townhouse taper sconce, amazon)
sources.mount_height: wall sconce mounted within 60-72 in = 1.52-1.83 m (1800lighting.com); 66 in = 1.68 m is the range midpoint — a PLACEMENT height, not a bound

chandelier.source: chandelier diameter ~1/2-2/3 table width (megcohomes.com; lightopia.com); medieval candle-corona

sources.diameter: chandelier ~1/2 to 2/3 the table width; for a ~1 m tavern table -> ~0.5-0.6 m (megcohomes.com; lightopia.com)
sources.hang_height: bottom of a dining chandelier 66-76 in = 1.68-1.93 m from the floor; ~1.85 m midpoint (megcohomes.com) — a PLACEMENT height, not a bound (the 7 ft figure is for entry halls with no table)
sources._note: medieval halls/churches used hanging candle coronas (period-appropriate)

mug.source: pint pewter tankard 127-140 mm (englishpewter.com; studioburkedc.com); beer stein 14 cm (dimensions.com)

sources.height: pint pewter tankard 130 mm (englishpewter.com straight-body); ~127 mm / 'a little over 5 in' (studioburkedc.com); beer stein 140 mm / 5.5 in (dimensions.com/element/beer-stein). Range 127-140 mm; target 130 mm.
sources.width: tankard/stein dia ~80-95 mm (englishpewter.com 8 cm; dimensions.com beer-stein 9.5 cm)
sources._note: PERIOD-APPROPRIATE: wooden treen mugs / leather blackjacks / pewter tankards all medieval. Microcube floor (1/9 m) -> a single 0.11 m block.

bottle.source: standard 750 ml wine bottle 30 cm x 7.5 cm (dimensions.com)

sources.height: standard 750 ml wine bottle 11.8 in = 30 cm (dimensions.com/element/wine-bottle-750-ml-standard)
sources._note: MILD ANACHRONISM: glass bottles became common ~17th c; the medieval drink vessel = ceramic jug / leather bottell / costrel. Kept as a fantasy-tavern prop. Microcube floor -> 1 wide x 3 tall column.
